verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas offers several exit paths: plan-listed 'Project Archive and Restore' and 'Download Apps for Self-hosting', a REST API, and playcanvas-sync for mirroring project assets to the local filesystem. The MIT open-source engine means downloaded apps can run without the vendor, and SplatTransform/SuperSplat convert and export splat data between formats. However, the evidence never says the Editor project archive itself is in a documented open format, these features are plan-listed (possibly gated), and community reports describe code living on PlayCanvas servers as a lock-in risk. Missing for 10: documentation of the project archive's format and how complete it is, confirmation that export is available on all plans, and hands-on corroboration of a full export-and-leave migration.
